description: Debes discutir con un coordinador académico sobre las condiciones de tu beca doctoral para asegurar que se alineen con tus necesidades de investigación.
objective: Convencer al coordinador (Dr. Matthews) de que aumente tu asignación mensual de 800 a 1000 euros, añada 2 meses de prórroga al contrato de 36 meses, y asegure acceso garantizado a los equipos del laboratorio de microscopía antes de septiembre, justificando cada petición con argumentos académicos concretos.
scene_context: Estás en la oficina del Dr. Matthews, coordinador de investigación doctoral en una universidad británica, después de que te haya notificado cambios en la financiación disponible.
expected_outcome_indicator: Secure increased funding, contract extension, and lab access guarantees through reasoned negotiation.
example_conversation:
Person: I appreciate your time today. As you know, we're facing some budgetary constraints across the doctoral scheme this year, which means we may need to revisit certain allocations.
User: I understand the fiscal pressures, Dr. Matthews, but I'd like to present a case for why the additional 200 euros monthly wouldn't merely constitute a personal convenience—it's essential for conducting rigorous fieldwork in my methodology.
Person: I'm listening, though I should mention that any adjustment would need to be offset by demonstrable gains in productivity or publication trajectory.
User: Precisely my point. The supplementary funds would enable me to secure access to the tissue samples repository at the biotech facility, which, whilst technically available, requires a licensing fee that my current allocation simply doesn't accommodate—without it, my comparative analysis becomes untenable.
Person: That's a more compelling rationale than I'd anticipated. As for the contract extension, that's considerably trickier given the departmental mandate.
User: I recognise the constraints, yet if I might respectfully suggest: postponing the completion date by merely two months would align my thesis submission with the spring publication cycle, thereby maximising the department's research output when it comes to the annual review metrics—not to mention that it mitigates the risk of rushed conclusions.

title: Impugnar una evaluación de desempeño laboral
description: Cuestionas una calificación injusta en tu evaluación anual y solicitas una revisión basada en evidencia concreta.
objective: Debes impugnar la evaluación de desempeño recibida el 15 de marzo argumentando que tus logros (incremento de ventas del 23%, liderazgo de 3 proyectos exitosos y reducción de costos de $50,000) no se reflejan en la calificación "satisfactorio", y solicitar explícitamente una reclasificación a "excepcional" o una revisión por un tercero en las próximas dos semanas.
scene_context: Estás en la oficina de tu manager, Sarah Chen, después de recibir tu evaluación anual. La tensión es evidente pero profesional.
expected_outcome_indicator: Successfully challenge unfair appraisal with documented evidence and negotiate review timeline.
example_conversation:
Person: I've reviewed your annual evaluation, and while your contributions have been solid, we felt your initiative has been somewhat limited this cycle.
User: I appreciate your feedback, but I'm afraid I must respectfully contest that characterization. Not only did I spearhead the market expansion initiative that yielded a 23% revenue uptick, but I also mitigated significant procurement bottlenecks, which netted us $50,000 in cost savings—metrics that are, frankly, difficult to reconcile with a "satisfactory" rating.
Person: Well, those are certainly notable achievements, but we need to see more strategic thinking and cross-departmental collaboration.
User: With respect, I led three cross-functional projects this year, all of which concluded ahead of schedule and within budget. I'm concerned that the evaluation doesn't accurately reflect the quantifiable outcomes. I'd like to request an expedited review—either by yourself with additional documentation, or by an independent third party within the next two weeks—to ensure the assessment aligns with the evidence.
Person: That's a fair point. I'll discuss it with upper management and get back to you by Friday.
User: Thank you. I appreciate your willingness to reconsider, and I'm confident that once you examine the project reports and stakeholder feedback, the discrepancy will become evident.

title: Defender tu argumento sobre un cambio de estructura organizacional en tu empresa
description: Tu empresa ha reorganizado los departamentos y tú debes defender la viabilidad de una propuesta alternativa ante el director ejecutivo.
objective: Debes argumentar que el nuevo modelo centralizado perjudicará la retención de talento (ya han renunciado 3 empleados senior en 2 meses), aumentará el tiempo de respuesta a clientes de 24 a 72 horas, y afectará la productividad del equipo de tu división en un 35% según tus proyecciones. Propone mantener 2 equipos descentralizados con supervisión coordinada, requiriendo un presupuesto adicional de 80.000€ anuales pero generando ahorros de 250.000€ evitando rotación de personal.
scene_context: Estás en una reunión de junta directiva con la CEO, Margaret Chen, quien ya implementó la reestructuración hace 3 semanas sin retroalimentación.
expected_outcome_indicator: Presented compelling ROI argument grounded in attrition data and operational metrics, challenging centralization strategy with feasible decentralized alternative.
example_conversation:
Person: The restructuring is already in motion, and I'm confident it will yield significant efficiencies. I'm not sure what prompted you to revisit this now, frankly.
User: I respect the decision, but the data from the first three weeks warrants a reconsideration; we've already lost three senior team members, and our customer response time has ballooned from 24 to 72 hours—figures that directly contradict the efficiency promise.
Person: These are early growing pains; people adapt, and we'll optimize response protocols as we go.
User: Granted that adjustment periods are inevitable, yet the attrition pattern is alarming when contextualized against industry benchmarks; replacing a mid-level analyst costs roughly 150 percent of their annual salary, so three departures alone have cost us 320.000€ in recruitment and onboarding—a figure that rather undercuts any savings the centralization was meant to achieve.
Person: You're conflating separate issues; attrition happens regardless of structure.
User: Perhaps in the abstract, but my proposal isn't to jettison the restructuring wholesale; rather, it's to maintain two decentralized hubs with coordinated oversight, which would require 80.000€ additional annually but would likely prevent future attrition and restore client responsiveness, thereby netting a 250.000€ saving relative to the costs of turnover we're currently incurring.

title: Cuestionar una política de crédito corporativo restrictiva
description: Negocias con tu director financiero sobre la revisión de los criterios de acceso a fondos discrecionales para proyectos innovadores.
objective: Debes convencer al director de que amplíe los límites de crédito discrecional de $50,000 a $150,000 para tu departamento, argumentando que los criterios actuales son demasiado rigurosos y limitan la competitividad de la empresa en el mercado.
scene_context: Estás en la oficina del director financiero de una empresa multinacional. Necesitas justificar por qué la política actual es contraproducente para la estrategia de innovación.
expected_outcome_indicator: Persuade Director to reconsider discretionary spending limits through reasoned argumentation.
example_conversation:
Person: I appreciate your proposal, but frankly, the current thresholds have been in place for precisely this reason—to mitigate frivolous expenditure. What makes you think loosening them would benefit rather than compromise our fiscal prudence?
User: I understand your concern about fiscal discipline, but I'd argue the criteria are so restrictive that we're inadvertently handicapping ourselves relative to competitors who move faster on emerging opportunities. The $50,000 ceiling, which hasn't been indexed since 2019, effectively prevents us from piloting technologies that could yield substantial ROI within eighteen months.
Person: Those are rather broad claims. Do you have empirical evidence that our caution is costing us market share, or are you largely speculating?
User: Not entirely—I've analyzed three quarters of rejected proposals that would've fallen into the $50,000 to $150,000 band, and eighteen percent of them addressed client pain points our competitors subsequently captured. Granted, not all would have succeeded, but the opportunity cost of blanket rejection far exceeds the downside risk of selective, monitored access to those funds.
Person: You make a fair point, though I'd need to see that analysis in detail before committing to anything. Let's say I'm willing to entertain a pilot phase—perhaps with stricter governance mechanisms and quarterly reviews rather than an outright increase.
User: That's a constructive approach, and I'm genuinely grateful. I'd propose we trial this with a $100,000 threshold for Q3 and Q4, coupled with a steering committee that vets proposals against predefined innovation criteria. If the metrics validate the hypothesis—adoption rates, cost savings, or new revenue streams—we revisit the permanent threshold thereafter.

title: Defender tu posición en un debate ético corporativo
description: Participas en una reunión de stakeholders donde debes argumentar una posición matizada sobre responsabilidad social empresarial frente a presiones financieras.
objective: Debes explicar por qué tu empresa debería invertir 2,5 millones de euros en prácticas sostenibles durante los próximos 18 meses, a pesar de que reducirá márgenes de ganancia en un 8%, reconociendo simultáneamente las preocupaciones de los accionistas sobre dividendos trimestrales y competitividad de mercado.
scene_context: Estás en una sala de juntas con el director financiero y tres miembros del consejo asesor que cuestionan tus propuestas de sostenibilidad. Necesitas persuadir sin sonar ingenuo.
expected_outcome_indicator: Successfully balanced ethical imperative with business reality and secured cautious consideration.
example_conversation:
Person: Look, I appreciate the sentiment, but frankly, sinking €2.5 million into sustainability initiatives when our competitors are cutting costs seems tone-deaf to shareholder concerns. What's your contingency if this doesn't yield ROI within three years?
User: I understand the trepidation, and you're right to raise it. However, what I'm proposing isn't altruism divorced from strategy; it's a calculated hedge against regulatory liability and reputational risk, both of which, as you know, have increasingly tangible financial implications. The €2.5 million represents a discretionary allocation that, mitigated through phased procurement and operational efficiency gains, would effectively cost us 4.2% rather than the full 8%.
Person: Phased, you say? Walk me through the timeline and where you'd absorb the losses initially.
User: Precisely. Q1 and Q2 focus on supply-chain audits and vendor renegotiation—minimal outlay. By Q3, we transition to carbon-neutral logistics, which admittedly incurs upfront costs, but the long-term savings on energy procurement offset roughly 60% by month eighteen. As for the remaining 40%, that's where reputational capital and risk mitigation converge; institutional investors increasingly penalize opacity on ESG metrics.
Person: And if the market doesn't reward that posture?
User: Then we've still fortified ourselves against what's now virtually inevitable regulatory tightening, whilst our competitors scramble to retrofit. We're not betting on virtue signalling; we're inoculating the firm.

title: Escalación de queja grave a gestión superior
description: Necesitas elevar una reclamación de seguridad laboral seria al director general después de que tu supervisora inmediata rechazó múltiples reportes sobre un equipo defectuoso.
objective: Debes documentar e informar al director general que durante 6 semanas has reportado malfuncionamiento crítico en la maquinaria de la línea 3, presentar evidencia de tres incidentes sin lesiones graves, e insistir en una auditoría independiente de seguridad antes del 15 de enero, sin acusar directamente a tu supervisora de negligencia deliberada.
scene_context: Estás en el despacho del director general en una fábrica de manufactura. Tu supervisora directa no está presente. El director general te conoce de vista pero no íntimamente.
expected_outcome_indicator: Escalation accepted, independent safety audit scheduled, documented complaint formally recorded.
example_conversation:
Person: Your supervisor mentioned you've raised some concerns about Line 3. I've reviewed her assessment and she seems confident the equipment is within tolerance. What specifically are we discussing here?
User: With respect, sir, I believe there's a discrepancy in how the data's been interpreted. I've documented three instances—November 8th, 12th, and December 3rd—where the hydraulic coupling has misfired, each time creating momentary pressure spikes that, fortunately, haven't yet resulted in serious injury. However, what troubles me is the trajectory: the incidents are increasing in frequency, and my supervisor, though conscientious, may be deferring to manufacturer specifications rather than observable degradation.
Person: You're suggesting she's been dismissive, then.
User: I'm suggesting, sir, that there may be an institutional blind spot—not malice, but perhaps an over-reliance on the equipment's certification history. I've requested a formal maintenance log review three times. What I'm asking is for an independent third-party safety audit before we resume full-capacity production. The liability exposure, frankly, is significant.
Person: Independent audit is expensive and signals doubt about our protocols.
User: Understandably. However, the cost of a single serious injury—both human and legal—would dwarf the audit expenditure many times over. I'm not asking to shut down; I'm asking for verification. If the equipment passes, everyone sleeps better. If it doesn't, we've averted a catastrophe. That's not hyperbole; it's prudent governance.

title: Entrevista senior: argumentar experiencia no convencional
description: Entrevista para un puesto de director de operaciones donde tu carrera ha sido marcada por rotaciones y relevos laterales en lugar de una trayectoria lineal ascendente.
objective: Debes explicar cómo tus 12 años en tres empresas diferentes, con cambios de rol cada 3-4 años, te han preparado mejor para este puesto de director de operaciones que un candidato con ascenso lineal, mencionando específicamente el aprendizaje adquirido en gestión de cambio organizacional, adaptabilidad cultural y pensamiento sistémico.
scene_context: Estás en una entrevista con la directora de RRHH y el CEO de una empresa de tecnología mediana. Ambos han hecho una pregunta directa sobre la falta de linealidad en tu currículum.
expected_outcome_indicator: Reframed career narrative as strategic asset; demonstrated meta-competence in organizational complexity.
example_conversation:
Person: I'll be candid—your CV shows three companies in twelve years, lateral moves rather than progression. Some hiring managers might interpret that as restlessness or inability to commit. How do you see it?
User: Fair question, and I appreciate the directness. What appears as lateral movement is actually deliberately curated exposure to different operational architectures. Each transition wasn't flight; it was strategic infiltration of a new ecosystem. At TechCore, I optimized supply-chain procurement; at Nordic, I restructured customer operations for a distributed model; at Ascent, I navigated a post-acquisition integration where two entirely different cultures had to coalesce.
Person: So you're framing instability as intentional learning. But how does that translate to staying put and delivering in this role?
User: Because what I've acquired isn't just technical acumen—it's immunity to institutional inertia. Most directors of operations inherit a system and tweak it. I've built systems from misaligned fragments. I understand not just *how* operations function, but *why* they resist change, and critically, which resistance is structural versus cultural. When you inherit a role in a growing firm, you won't need someone who optimizes yesterday's paradigm; you'll need someone who can diagnose why stakeholders disagree on what optimization even means.
Person: That's elegant, but it's still a bet on someone who hasn't held a position longer than four years.
User: True. But consider: I'm not asking you to bet on loyalty to a title; I'm asking you to leverage someone whose liability *is* their ability to operate across organizational fractures. In eighteen months, you'll have clarity on whether that's valuable or whether you need institutional continuity. Either way, you'll have de-risked the decision through my track record of successful integrations.

title: Negociar los términos de un contrato de suministro
description: Debes defender tu posición sobre los plazos de entrega y las cláusulas de responsabilidad en una reunión con el proveedor senior.
objective: Lograr reducir el período de entrega de 90 a 60 días, limitar la responsabilidad máxima a €50,000 y asegurar que se incluya una cláusula de fuerza mayor que exima a ambas partes en caso de circunstancias impredecibles.

expected_outcome_indicator: Successfully negotiated delivery timeline, liability cap, and force majeure clause.
example_conversation:
Person: I appreciate your concerns, but I must emphasize that our standard terms reflect industry norms and mitigate our exposure considerably. Frankly, reducing the delivery window to sixty days would necessitate restructuring our entire supply chain, which frankly isn't discretionary for us.
User: I understand the constraints, yet what you're characterizing as industry standard doesn't align with what we're seeing elsewhere. Moreover, if we're to commit to a three-year contract of this magnitude, we need the flexibility that a sixty-day window provides, particularly given the volatility in our sector.
Person: That's a fair point, though I'd argue that the liability cap of one hundred thousand is precisely calibrated to compensate for unforeseen disruptions without bankrupting us operationally.
User: That's where I must respectfully push back. A hundred thousand doesn't adequately reflect the scale of our potential losses, nor does it incentivize the quality assurance we're investing in. What if we compromise at fifty thousand, but only if we include a robust force majeure clause that protects both parties?
Person: You're not wrong that a force majeure provision would assuage certain concerns. I could potentially advocate internally for seventy-five days and fifty thousand if you're amenable to accepting the liability as written.
User: That's movement, and I appreciate it. Seventy-five days is workable, provided we lock in the fifty thousand cap and ensure the force majeure language explicitly covers supply chain disruptions, which frankly, is increasingly relevant given geopolitical uncertainties we've all witnessed.

title: Negociar cláusulas de un contrato de obra con un arquitecto
description: Explicar tus preocupaciones sobre términos contractuales ambiguos en un proyecto de renovación residencial.
objective: Cuestionar al menos tres cláusulas específicas del contrato (plazos de entrega, responsabilidad por daños materiales, y mecanismo de resolución de disputas) y solicitar enmiendas concretas antes de firmar por €85,000.
scene_context: Estás en la oficina de un arquitecto renombrado tras recibir un borrador de contrato para la renovación de tu propiedad. Necesitas aclarar términos que consideras onerosos.
expected_outcome_indicator: Successfully challenge vague contract terms and propose three concrete amendments.
example_conversation:
Person: Well, I've drafted a fairly standard agreement for the full renovation, which as you know encompasses the structural assessment, interior redesign, and project management through to completion.
User: I appreciate the comprehensiveness, but I'm concerned about the liability clause—specifically section 4.3, which appears to place all responsibility for unforeseen structural damage exclusively on my shoulders, despite my having engaged your firm precisely to mitigate such risks. Could we redefine that?
Person: That clause is fairly boilerplate in the industry, though I understand your apprehension. What sort of amendment were you envisioning?
User: I'd propose a tiered liability model whereby structural issues attributable to poor initial assessment fall under your purview, whereas those stemming from pre-existing conditions I failed to disclose remain mine. Additionally, the delivery timeline is vague—would you be amenable to inserting penalty clauses for overruns beyond three months?
Person: Penalty clauses do add complexity, but they're not unreasonable given the €85,000 investment involved. However, I'd need to insert a force majeure clause to protect us both from unforeseen circumstances.
User: Absolutely, provided we define force majeure narrowly to exclude supply chain delays, which are rather predictable in this market. That brings me to my third concern: the dispute resolution mechanism. Rather than litigation, might we include mandatory mediation before proceeding to arbitration?

title: Reclamar un pedido que llegó tarde
description: Tu pedido lleva dos semanas sin llegar.
objective: Da el número de pedido, explica el retraso y pide una solución o el reembolso.

Support Agent: Can you give me the order number?
User: Yes, it is 4-5-8-2-1.
Support Agent: I am sorry. The package is lost. Do you want a refund?
User: Yes, please. A refund is better.

title: Apuntarse a un curso de cocina
description: Ves un curso de cocina italiana y preguntas detalles.
objective: Pregunta los días, el precio y si hace falta llevar delantal, y reserva una plaza.
scene_context: Estás en la recepción de una escuela de cocina. Huele a pan recién hecho.
example_conversation:
Course Coordinator: Hello! I am interested in the Italian cooking course.
User: It is on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
Course Coordinator: What time does it start?
User: At six in the evening. It costs fifty euros.
Course Coordinator: Do I need to bring an apron?
User: No, we give you one. Do you want to book a place?
Course Coordinator: Yes, please. My name is Ana.

title: Abrir una cuenta en el banco
description: Quieres una cuenta para tu primer trabajo.
objective: Pide abrir una cuenta, pregunta qué documentos necesitas y cuánto tarda la tarjeta.
scene_context: Estás en una oficina bancaria sentado frente a un empleado.
example_conversation:
Bank Clerk: Good morning! I would like to open an account.
User: Of course. Do you have your ID card?
Bank Clerk: Yes, here it is.
User: And a certificate of your address.
Bank Clerk: I have it too. How long does the card take?
User: One week, and you can use the app today.

title: Pedir comida a domicilio
description: Llamas al restaurante para pedir la cena.
objective: Pide una pizza y una ensalada, da tu dirección y pregunta cuánto tarda el reparto.
scene_context: Estás en casa con hambre. Llamas al restaurante italiano de la esquina.
example_conversation:
Restaurant Host: Good evening, Bella Pizza.
User: Hello, I would like to order some food.
Restaurant Host: What would you like?
User: A pizza and a salad, please.
Restaurant Host: What is your address?
User: Number five, Green street. How long does it take?
Restaurant Host: Thirty minutes.
User: Perfect, thank you.

title: Perder el vuelo
description: Llegas tarde y tu vuelo acaba de salir.
objective: Explica lo que ha pasado, pide otro vuelo para hoy y pregunta si hay coste extra.
scene_context: Estás en el mostrador de la aerolínea, sudando y con la maleta.
example_conversation:
Airline Agent: Hello, I missed my flight to Rome.
User: What time was your flight?
Airline Agent: At eleven, but the taxi was late.
User: There is another flight at four.
Airline Agent: Is there an extra cost?
User: There is a change fee of thirty euros.
Airline Agent: OK, I will take it.

title: Visitar a un compañero enfermo
description: Tu compañero está en casa con gripe.
objective: Pregunta cómo se siente, ofrécele sopa y dile que avisarás al equipo.
scene_context: Estás en casa de tu compañero con una bolsa de la compra.
example_conversation:
Sick Colleague: How do you feel today?
User: Better, but I still have a fever.
Sick Colleague: I brought you some soup.
User: Thank you! You did not have to.
Sick Colleague: Do you need anything from the shop?
User: No, thanks. Just rest.
Sick Colleague: I will tell the team you are ill.

title: Comprar un regalo para tu sobrino
description: Tu sobrino cumple ocho años.
objective: Pregunta por juguetes para un niño de ocho años y elige algo con envío a casa.
scene_context: Estás en una juguetería llena de colores. Una dependienta coloca cajas.
example_conversation:
Toy Shop Assistant: Hello! I am looking for a present for my nephew.
User: How old is he?
Toy Shop Assistant: He is eight. He loves building things.
User: This construction set is very popular.
Toy Shop Assistant: How much is it?
User: Twenty-five euros. Do you want it wrapped?
Toy Shop Assistant: Yes, please. It is for his birthday.

title: Alquilar un coche para el fin de semana
description: Quieres un coche para hacer una excursión.
objective: Alquila un coche pequeño desde el viernes, pregunta por el seguro y el combustible.
scene_context: Estás en el mostrador de una empresa de alquiler de coches.
example_conversation:
Rental Agent: Hello! I would like to rent a car for the weekend.
User: A small car or a big one?
Rental Agent: A small one, please. From Friday to Sunday.
User: It is eighty euros with full insurance.
Rental Agent: Is the petrol included?
User: No, you return it full.
Rental Agent: OK, that is fine.

title: Preguntar por el wifi del hotel
description: No consigues conectar el móvil.
objective: Pide la contraseña del wifi, pregunta si es gratis y si llega a las habitaciones.
scene_context: Estás en la recepción del hotel con el móvil en la mano.
example_conversation:
Hotel Receptionist: Good evening. What is the wifi password?
User: It is on your key card, but I can tell you: blue-2-0-2-4.
Hotel Receptionist: Is it free?
User: Yes, it is free for all guests.
Hotel Receptionist: Does it work in the rooms?
User: Yes, and also in the restaurant.

title: Hablar con el casero de una avería
description: Se ha roto la caldera en pleno invierno.
objective: Explica que no hay agua caliente, pide un técnico hoy y pregunta quién paga la reparación.
scene_context: Estás en el salón con el teléfono. Hace frío y la caldera no enciende.
example_conversation:
Landlord: Hello, this is Ana from flat three.
User: Hello Ana, is everything OK?
Landlord: No, the boiler is broken. There is no hot water.
User: I am sorry. I will call a technician today.
Landlord: Can he come before six? I work in the morning.
User: Yes, I will tell him. The repair is on me.
Landlord: Thank you very much.

title: Primer contacto para un trabajo de verano
description: Vas a una entrevista rápida en una cafetería.
objective: Preséntate, di tu disponibilidad en verano y pregunta por las tareas del puesto.
scene_context: Estás de pie en la barra de una cafetería. El encargado limpia una taza.
example_conversation:
Café Manager: Hello! I am here about the summer job.
User: Great. Do you have any experience?
Café Manager: I worked in a bakery last summer.
User: When can you start?
Café Manager: In July. I am free every morning.
User: The job is serving coffee and cleaning tables.
Café Manager: That is fine for me.

title: Farmacia: jarabe para la tos
description: Tienes tos desde hace tres días.
objective: Pide un jarabe para la tos, pregunta la dosis para un adulto y si da sueño.
scene_context: Estás en la farmacia del barrio. El farmacéutico ordena cajas.
example_conversation:
Pharmacist: Good morning! I need something for a cough.
User: How long have you had it?
Pharmacist: For three days, and it is worse at night.
User: This syrup is good for that.
Pharmacist: How much do I take?
User: Two spoons three times a day.
Pharmacist: Does it make you sleepy?
User: A little, so take it at night.

title: Clase de prueba en el gimnasio
description: Quieres probar una clase de spinning.
objective: Pregunta el horario de spinning, pide una clase de prueba gratis y si hay taquillas.
scene_context: Estás en la recepción del gimnasio. Suena música con ritmo al fondo.
example_conversation:
Gym Receptionist: Hello! I want to try a spinning class.
User: We have classes at seven and eight.
Gym Receptionist: Can I try one for free?
User: Yes, the first class is free.
Gym Receptionist: Perfect. Are there lockers?
User: Yes, bring a padlock.
Gym Receptionist: See you at seven.

title: Cita en la peluquería
description: Necesitas un corte antes de una boda.
objective: Pide cita para el sábado, explica el corte que quieres y pregunta el precio con lavado.
scene_context: Estás en la puerta de una peluquería pequeña. La peluquera barre el suelo.
example_conversation:
Hairdresser: Hello! Do you have time on Saturday?
User: Yes, at eleven or at five.
Hairdresser: At eleven, please. I have a wedding.
User: How do you want the cut?
Hairdresser: Short on the sides, not too short on top.
User: With wash and dry, it is twenty euros.
Hairdresser: Perfect, see you Saturday.

title: Devolver libros a la biblioteca con retraso
description: Los libros llevan una semana de retraso.
objective: Explica el retraso, pregunta cuánto es la multa y renueva un libro si puedes.
scene_context: Estás en el mostrador de la biblioteca con tres libros.
example_conversation:
Librarian: Hello, I am returning these books. They are late.
User: Let me check... one week late.
Librarian: How much is the fine?
User: One euro per book, so three euros.
Librarian: Can I take this one again?
User: Yes, but you have to pay first.
Librarian: No problem. Here you go.

title: Organizar una barbacoa con amigos
description: El sábado hacéis una barbacoa en el parque.
objective: Reparte lo que lleva cada uno, confirma la hora y pregunta si hay mesa reservada.
scene_context: Estás en el parque con dos amigos organizando el sábado.
example_conversation:
Friend: So, what time on Saturday?
User: At one. I will reserve a table.
Friend: I can bring the meat and the bread.
User: Great. I will bring drinks and plates.
Friend: What about Marta?
User: She will bring a salad and some fruit.
Friend: Perfect. See you on Saturday!

title: Cambio de puerta de embarque
description: Tu puerta de embarque ha cambiado y no lo entiendes.
objective: Pregunta por tu puerta, comprueba la hora de embarque y pide indicaciones para llegar.
scene_context: Estás delante de un panel de vuelos en el aeropuerto con la tarjeta de embarque.
example_conversation:
Airport Staff: Excuse me, my gate changed. Where is gate C twenty?
User: Gate C twenty is in terminal two.
Airport Staff: How do I get to terminal two?
User: Take the shuttle bus, it is five minutes.
Airport Staff: What time is boarding?
User: Boarding starts at half past six.
Airport Staff: Thank you, I will run!

title: Comprar una estantería
description: Necesitas una estantería para tu salón.
objective: Pregunta medidas y precio, pide entrega a casa y si el montaje está incluido.
scene_context: Estás en una tienda de muebles con una cinta de medir en el bolsillo.
example_conversation:
Furniture Assistant: Hello! I am looking for a shelf for my living room.
User: What size do you need?
Furniture Assistant: Two metres wide and white.
User: This one is two metres and costs ninety euros.
Furniture Assistant: Do you deliver to your home?
User: Yes, for fifteen euros. Assembly is ten more.
Furniture Assistant: I will take it without assembly.

title: Dar parte al seguro del coche
description: Han rayado tu coche en el aparcamiento.
objective: Explica el daño, da la fecha y lugar, y pregunta cuánto tarda la reparación.
scene_context: Estás en casa llamando a tu seguro de coche con fotos del daño.
example_conversation:
Insurance Agent: Good morning, I want to report some damage to my car.
User: What happened?
Insurance Agent: Someone scratched it in the car park.
User: When was it?
Insurance Agent: Yesterday afternoon, at the shopping centre.
User: Send me the photos and the policy number.
Insurance Agent: How long does the repair take?
User: About four days.

title: Negociar la subida del alquiler
description: El casero quiere subir el alquiler un 8%.
objective: Discute la subida con argumentos, propón un aumento menor y pide un acuerdo por escrito.
scene_context: Estás sentado en el salón con el casero y el contrato sobre la mesa.
example_conversation:
Landlord: As you know, I would like to raise the rent this year.
User: I understand prices are going up, but eight percent is a lot.
Landlord: The building costs have increased too.
User: Could we agree on four percent instead?
Landlord: Four percent is very low for me.
User: What about five, and I take care of the garden?
Landlord: That sounds reasonable. Five percent it is.
User: Great. Could you send it to me in writing?

title: Proponer cambiar la fecha del proyecto
description: El equipo no llegará al viernes con la entrega.
objective: Explica el retraso con datos, propón mover la entrega al martes y pide confirmación.
scene_context: Estás en una sala de reuniones con el equipo y un calendario en la pizarra.
example_conversation:
Project Lead: We have a problem with Friday.
User: How serious is it?
Project Lead: Two people are ill and we are behind schedule.
User: How much time do we need?
Project Lead: Two more days. I suggest Tuesday at noon.
User: The client will not like it, but it is realistic.
Project Lead: I will call them and explain the situation.
User: Good. Could you copy me in the email?

title: Entrevista de trabajo: experiencia
description: Estás en una entrevista para un puesto de oficina.
objective: Habla de tu experiencia anterior con ejemplos, explica por qué te interesa el puesto y pregunta por el equipo.
scene_context: Estás en una sala pequeña frente a la responsable de contratación.
example_conversation:
Recruiter: Tell me a little about your experience.
User: I worked for two years in customer support.
Recruiter: What did you learn there?
User: I learned to solve problems calmly and work with deadlines.
Recruiter: Why do you want this job?
User: I want to grow in a bigger team and learn from them.
Recruiter: How do you work under pressure?
User: I organise my tasks by priority and communicate early.

title: Reclamar una factura del teléfono
description: Tu factura es el doble de lo normal.
objective: Pide explicación de los cargos extra, rechaza el cobro si es un error y pide una revisión por escrito.
scene_context: Estás llamando a la compañía telefónica con la factura delante.
example_conversation:
Support Agent: Good morning, how can I help you?
User: My bill this month is double the usual amount.
Support Agent: Let me check... There is a charge for extra data.
User: That cannot be right. I have been using wifi all month.
Support Agent: It may be an error in the system.
User: I would like a review, and I am not paying that part.
Support Agent: I will open a case and send you the result by email.
User: Thank you. Please also confirm it in writing today.

title: Vuelo retrasado: pedir compensación
description: Tu vuelo se retrasó seis horas y quieres compensación.
objective: Pide explicación del retraso, menciona tus derechos y solicita la compensación y una noche de hotel.
scene_context: Estás en el mostrador de la aerolínea con la tarjeta de embarque.
example_conversation:
Airline Agent: Good evening. How can I help you?
User: My flight was delayed six hours and I missed my connection.
Airline Agent: I am sorry. We can offer you a hotel for tonight.
User: Thank you, but I would also like to claim compensation.
Airline Agent: Under the rules, that depends on the reason for the delay.
User: The reason was technical, so I believe I am entitled.
Airline Agent: You can fill in this form and we will answer in two weeks.
User: Fine. Could you give me a copy of the form?

title: Hábitos saludables con un entrenador
description: Quieres mejorar tu rutina de ejercicio y descanso.
objective: Explica tu rutina actual, acepta consejos concretos y acuerda un plan de dos semanas.
scene_context: Estás en el gimnasio con un entrenador y una libreta de seguimiento.
example_conversation:
Personal Trainer: How many times a week do you exercise now?
User: Once or twice, and I sleep badly.
Personal Trainer: Sleep is as important as training.
User: I know, but I finish work very late.
Personal Trainer: Try three short sessions and no screens after ten.
User: That sounds possible. What about food?
Personal Trainer: More vegetables and water, less sugar at night.
User: OK. Can we check the plan again in two weeks?

title: Organizar un viaje en grupo
description: El grupo no se pone de acuerdo con el destino.
objective: Escucha las dos opciones, propón un criterio de decisión y cierra un acuerdo con fechas.
scene_context: Estás en un café con dos amigos discutiendo el viaje de verano.
example_conversation:
Friend: I still think the mountains are cheaper.
User: True, but the beach has more activities.
Friend: The beach hotels are full in August.
User: Then why do not we go in the first week of July?
Friend: I cannot take those days, I have a course.
User: What if we decide by budget? Everyone sends a number.
Friend: That is fair. We can vote on Friday.
User: Agreed. I will create a group to share prices.

title: Devolver un producto defectuoso
description: Los auriculares que compraste no cargan.
objective: Explica el defecto, pide un reembolso y rechaza un vale si la ley te da la razón.
scene_context: Estás en el mostrador de una tienda de electrónica con la caja y el recibo.
example_conversation:
Store Manager: Good afternoon. How can I help you?
User: These headphones do not charge. I bought them last week.
Store Manager: Did you try another cable?
User: Yes, and another charger. The problem is the product.
Store Manager: I can offer you a voucher for the shop.
User: I would prefer a refund, as is my right within fourteen days.
Store Manager: You are right. Let me process the refund.
User: Thank you. Could you keep a copy of the receipt?

title: Médico: estrés y mal sueño
description: Llevas semanas durmiendo mal por el trabajo.
objective: Describe los síntomas con detalle, pregunta por hábitos antes de medicación y pide una revisión.
scene_context: Estás en la consulta del médico después de varias noches sin dormir bien.
example_conversation:
Doctor: What brings you here today?
User: I have not been sleeping well for three weeks.
Doctor: How many hours do you sleep, more or less?
User: Four or five, and I wake up at night thinking about work.
Doctor: Do you drink coffee or use screens late?
User: Both. I finish work at eleven and check emails in bed.
Doctor: Before any medicine, let us change those habits for ten days.
User: Fine. Could we have another appointment after that?

title: Presentar una idea en clase
description: Expones una propuesta sobre reciclaje en tu escuela.
objective: Presenta tu idea, responde a dos preguntas y acuerda el siguiente paso con la clase.
scene_context: Estás de pie delante de tu clase con una presentación sencilla en la pizarra.
example_conversation:
Teacher: So, what is your proposal?
User: I suggest three more recycling bins and a poster campaign.
Teacher: Why do you think bins are the problem?
User: Because the survey shows students want to recycle but it is not easy.
Teacher: How much would it cost?
User: Around two hundred euros, and the posters can be designed here.
Teacher: Who would check that it works?
User: A small group of volunteers, with results every month.

title: Resolver un malentendido con un amigo
description: Tu amigo cree que no le invitaste a la cena.
objective: Aclara lo ocurrido sin discutir, discúlpate por el malentendido e invítale a repetir la cena.
scene_context: Estás en un restaurante con tu amigo. Hay tensión en el ambiente.
example_conversation:
Friend: I saw the photos of the dinner. Nobody told me about it.
User: I am really sorry. It was a last-minute thing.
Friend: I felt left out, to be honest.
User: I understand, and I should have called you first.
Friend: It is not only this time, you know.
User: You are right. I have been careless with our plans.
Friend: I just want to count on you when it matters.
User: You can. Let me invite you to dinner on Friday to fix this.

title: Renovar el alquiler con una mejora
description: Renuevas el contrato y pides pintar el piso.
objective: Acepta renovar, pide que pinten el salón y negocia quién paga los materiales.
scene_context: Estás en el salón con el casero revisando el contrato nuevo.
example_conversation:
Landlord: So, do you want to stay for another year?
User: Yes, I am happy here. But the living room needs paint.
Landlord: The last tenant left the walls quite bad, that is true.
User: Could the painting be included in the renewal?
Landlord: I can pay for half of the materials if you organise it.
User: Deal. I also want to fix the kitchen tap.
Landlord: Send me the numbers and I will approve them.
User: Perfect. When can we sign the new contract?

title: Cargo duplicado en el banco
description: Te han cobrado dos veces la misma compra.
objective: Señala el cargo duplicado, pide la devolución inmediata y pregunta cuánto tarda en llegar.
scene_context: Estás en la oficina del banco mostrando el movimiento en la app.
example_conversation:
Bank Clerk: Good morning. How can I help you?
User: This shop charged me twice for the same purchase.
Bank Clerk: When did it happen?
User: On Tuesday, and I only bought one item.
Bank Clerk: I can open a dispute with the shop for you.
User: How long does the refund take?
Bank Clerk: Between five and ten working days.
User: Please send me the case number by email.

title: Curso con requisitos
description: El curso que quieres pide un nivel mínimo.
objective: Comprueba si cumples los requisitos, pregunta cómo acreditar tu nivel y reserva plaza si es posible.
scene_context: Estás en la oficina de una escuela de idiomas con folletos y exámenes de prueba.
example_conversation:
Course Adviser: I want to join the advanced course.
User: It requires a B1 certificate or a level test.
Course Adviser: I do not have the certificate, but I use English at work.
User: Then you can take our test. It takes forty minutes.
Course Adviser: Is the test free if I then book the course?
User: Yes, and the result is valid for one year.
Course Adviser: Good. Can I take it on Thursday evening?
User: Yes, at six. I will reserve a place for you.

title: Orientación de estudios
description: No sabes qué estudiar el año que viene.
objective: Explica tus intereses y notas, escucha dos opciones y acuerda investigar una carrera concreta.
scene_context: Estás en el despacho del orientador con tus notas y una lista de intereses.
example_conversation:
School Counsellor: I do not know what to study next year.
User: Tell me two subjects you enjoy.
School Counsellor: Biology and maths, but I also like writing.
User: Have you thought about health sciences or data science?
School Counsellor: I am worried about the maths level in data science.
User: There are introductory courses you can try first.
School Counsellor: That would help me decide. Where can I find them?
User: I will send you a list this week and we can meet again.

title: Pedir más horas en el trabajo
description: Quieres pasar de media jornada a completa.
objective: Pide el cambio de horario, justifica con resultados y propón una prueba de un mes.
scene_context: Estás en la oficina de tu jefa con tu horario y tus últimos resultados.
example_conversation:
Manager: You wanted to talk about your hours.
User: Yes. I would like to move to a full-time contract.
Manager: Why now?
User: My sales grew twenty percent in the last three months.
Manager: That is true, you are doing well.
User: I could also take the afternoon deliveries.
Manager: Let us try it for one month and review the numbers.
User: Perfect. Could we write the new hours in an email?

title: Normas del piso compartido
description: Un nuevo compañero se muda y hay que hablar de normas.
objective: Propón normas de limpieza y ruido, escucha las objeciones y acordad un horario común.
scene_context: Estás en la cocina del piso con tu nuevo compañero y el calendario de tareas.
example_conversation:
Flatmate: Should we talk about the house rules?
User: Yes, better now than later.
Flatmate: I suggest cleaning the kitchen every day in turns.
User: Every day is a lot. What about every two days?
Flatmate: OK, and no loud music after eleven.
User: I work late some days, so I will be quiet anyway.
Flatmate: And guests? I prefer to know before.
User: Fair. I will send a message in the group.

title: Entrevista en un hotel: turnos
description: Buscas trabajo de recepción con turnos rotativos.
objective: Pregunta los turnos, explica tu disponibilidad y negocia las noches de fin de semana.
scene_context: Estás en la oficina del hotel frente a la jefa de recepción.
example_conversation:
Front Desk Manager: The job has rotating shifts, including nights.
User: How many nights per week?
Front Desk Manager: Two or three, and one weekend per month.
User: I can do nights, but I cannot work every Saturday.
Front Desk Manager: We can arrange one Saturday free each month.
User: That works for me. Do you provide training?
Front Desk Manager: Yes, one week with another receptionist.
User: Great. When would I start?

title: Reciclaje en el barrio
description: En tu calle no hay contenedores suficientes.
objective: Presenta el problema en la reunión de vecinos, propón una solución y ofrece encargarte del seguimiento.
scene_context: Estás en el salón comunitario con tus vecinos y un plano del barrio.
example_conversation:
Neighbourhood Chair: Neighbour, you wanted to raise a point?
User: Yes. There are only two recycling bins in the whole street.
Neighbourhood Chair: Do people use them?
User: They are full by Wednesday, so many bags end up on the ground.
Neighbourhood Chair: What do you suggest?
User: We could ask the council for two more and a small sign.
Neighbourhood Chair: Who writes the letter?
User: I can write it and collect signatures this week.

title: Preparar una entrevista con un mentor
description: Tienes una entrevista importante la semana que viene.
objective: Pide consejo sobre cómo responder a debilidades, ensaya una respuesta y acuerda una segunda práctica.
scene_context: Estás en una videollamada con tu mentor y tus notas de la oferta.
example_conversation:
Mentor: How do you feel about the interview?
User: Nervous. I do not know how to answer about weaknesses.
Mentor: Choose a real one and explain what you are doing about it.
User: For example, I used to speak too fast in meetings.
Mentor: Good. How did you solve it?
User: I prepare key points and pause before answering.
Mentor: That is a strong answer. Practise it once more.
User: OK. Can we do a full simulation on Monday?

title: Multa en el transporte público
description: Te han multado porque no validaste el billete.
objective: Explica que el billete era válido, pide revisar la multa y solicita presentar una reclamación formal.

Transport Officer: The inspector says you did not validate it.

Transport Officer: Do you have any proof?
User: Yes, a photo of the machine and the time of my trip.
Transport Officer: You can present a formal appeal within fifteen days.
User: I will do that. Could you give me the form and the reference?

title: Comprar un portátil: comparar opciones
description: Dudas entre dos modelos de portátil.
objective: Compara los dos modelos por memoria, batería y precio, y decide con el vendedor el más adecuado.

Tech Seller: I travel a lot, so the battery is important.

title: Hablar con el vecino del ruido
description: El vecino de arriba pone música hasta muy tarde.
objective: Expón el problema con calma, propón un horario razonable y acordad avisarse por mensaje.

example_conversation:

User: It will not happen again on weekdays.

Volunteer Coordinator: Do I need to bring anything?

title: Queja en el restaurante
description: Tu plato llegó frío y con retraso.
objective: Explica el problema sin perder la calma, pide una solución y acepta el postre de compensación.
scene_context: Estás en la mesa con el camarero y el plato a medio comer.
